original_question: A pure O-sequence is the h-vector of a pure monomial order ideal, and codimension is the number of variables in the ambient polynomial ring. For a fixed codimension r, what is the largest type t for which every pure O-sequence of codimension r is unimodal?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Open Problem 2: "For a fixed codimension r, what is the largest type t for which all pure O-sequences are unimodal?" ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact target almost verbatim: it asks the fixed-codimension/type-threshold unimodality problem that appears as Open Problem 2, and it correctly identifies a pure O-sequence as the h-vector of a pure monomial order ideal and codimension as the number of variables in the ambient polynomial ring. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
missing_details: The paper defines the type of a pure O-sequence as the number of maximal monomials in the pure monomial order ideal; equivalently, in the level-algebra formulation, it is the K-dimension of the socle. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, unimodal should be defined in the paper’s sense: weakly increasing up to some degree and then weakly decreasing thereafter. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

The quantifier is over all pure O-sequences of codimension r with no restriction on socle degree e; that arbitrariness is implicit in the open problem and should be stated explicitly. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

The phrase "largest type t" is slightly ambiguous as written; the surrounding discussion shows the intended threshold interpretation is: determine which types force unimodality for fixed codimension, i.e. all types up to that threshold. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

If one uses the algebraic formulation from Section 2, one should specify standard graded Artinian monomial level algebras A = K[x1, ..., xr]/I with I homogeneous and containing no nonzero linear forms, so that codimension equals r and the socle is concentrated in one degree. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

Section 2 also records the inverse-system equivalence via contraction, which is the paper’s bridge between pure monomial order ideals and Artinian monomial level algebras; your draft omits this equivalent setup. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

The paper notes that although some Weak Lefschetz arguments are characteristic-0 tools, the shape question for monomial Hilbert functions is characteristic-free, so the problem itself does not depend on the field K. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
refined_question: Fix a codimension r. Let h = (1, h1, ..., he) be a pure O-sequence in r variables, i.e. the h-vector of a pure monomial order ideal in K[y1, ..., yr], where e is arbitrary and the type is the number of maximal monomials. Determine the largest threshold t = t(r) such that every pure O-sequence of codimension r and type at most t is unimodal, where unimodal means weakly increasing up to some index and weakly decreasing thereafter. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, fix r and determine the largest threshold t = t(r) such that for every standard graded Artinian monomial level algebra A = K[x1, ..., xr]/I with no nonzero linear forms and socle dimension at most t, the Hilbert function h_A is unimodal. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
justification: I selected Section 5, Open Problem 2 because it is the nearest official formulation and your draft matches it essentially word for word. I only sharpened what the paper leaves implicit: the meaning of type, the paper’s definition of unimodal, the fact that socle degree is unrestricted, and the threshold reading of "largest type" suggested by the nearby Section 2 discussion asking which types force unimodality for fixed codimension. That same discussion also gives the closest local evidence for the intended problem: in codimension 3 all type-3 pure O-sequences are strictly unimodal, in codimension 4 all type-2 pure O-sequences are strictly unimodal, and the smallest known nonunimodal codimension-3 example has type 14. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
